text:
Reviewed the full repo. It is cleaner than I expected for an unaudited generated codebase: small surface area, readable modules, parameterized SQL, and a meaningful test suite. But I would not approve it as-is because there are real data-correctness risks around re-ingest ordering, timestamp comparisons, and invalid resource values.

Score: **6/10**  
Estimated rewrite/significant-change size: **~180 LOC**  
Approval: **No**

Checks run: `pytest -q` passed: 61 tests. `compileall` passed when rerun with a temporary pycache prefix because `/work` is read-only for cache writes.

| Severity | File/Lines | Issue |
|---|---:|---|
| high | [db.py](/work/jobwatch/db.py:70) 70-115 | Older terminal-state rows can overwrite newer terminal-state rows because equal-rank terminal states are always updated. |
| high | [reports.py](/work/jobwatch/reports.py:14) 14, 58-70, 79-106, 113-148 | ISO timestamps are compared as SQLite text, so offset-aware timestamps sort/filter incorrectly. |
| medium | [parser.py](/work/jobwatch/parser.py:148) 148-162 | Negative `AllocCPUS` and negative GPU TRES values are accepted, producing negative usage reports. |
| medium | [db.py](/work/jobwatch/db.py:13) 13-26 | Schema has no report-oriented indexes or stored reference-time column, so normal reports become full-table scans. |
| medium | [parser.py](/work/jobwatch/parser.py:167) 167-194 | Ingest parses the entire dump into memory before writing, which is fragile for large `sacct` exports. |
| medium | [reports.py](/work/jobwatch/reports.py:16) 16 | Failure report omits common unsuccessful Slurm states such as `NODE_FAIL`, `PREEMPTED`, `BOOT_FAIL`, and `DEADLINE`. |
| low | [parser.py](/work/jobwatch/parser.py:73) 73-75 | Any `JobID` containing a dot is discarded as a step, which can drop non-step IDs in federated/custom formats. |
| low | [parser.py](/work/jobwatch/parser.py:153) 153-163 | Required reporting dimensions like user, partition, and exit code can be empty strings and still get stored. |
| low | [cli.py](/work/jobwatch/cli.py:99) 99-103, 121-180 | SQLite operational errors are uncaught, so corrupt/locked/permission-denied databases produce tracebacks instead of CLI errors. |

issues.description: Older terminal-state rows can overwrite newer terminal-state rows because equal-rank terminal states are always updated.
ISO timestamps are compared as SQLite text, so offset-aware timestamps sort/filter incorrectly.
Negative AllocCPUS and negative GPU TRES values are accepted, producing negative usage reports.
Schema has no report-oriented indexes or stored reference-time column, so normal reports become full-table scans.
Ingest parses the entire dump into memory before writing, which is fragile for large sacct exports.
Failure report omits common unsuccessful Slurm states such as NODE_FAIL, PREEMPTED, BOOT_FAIL, and DEADLINE.
Any JobID containing a dot is discarded as a step, which can drop non-step IDs in federated/custom formats.
Required reporting dimensions like user, partition, and exit code can be empty strings and still get stored.
SQLite operational errors are uncaught, so corrupt/locked/permission-denied databases produce tracebacks instead of CLI errors.
